0. FOREWORD
0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indizn Standards Institution on 2 November 1967, after the draft finalized by the Electronic Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. 0.2 This srandard prescribes the conditions and procedures for tests to bc conducted on cathode-ray oscilloscopes covering ranges between dc and 10 MC/S to determine their performance characteristics. The tcs:s prcscribed in this standard apply only to complete oscilloscopes aud no separate consideration for the component parts has been given. 0.2.1 Ti'his standard does not cover methods of measurements of special facilities provided in certain types of cathode-ray oscilloscopes, such as two separate inputs to the vertical deflection system, multitrace and timcdelay characteristics for radar work. 0.2.2 This standard does not also apply to special construction or particular purpose oscilloscopes, such as sampling oscilloscopes, vectorscopes and characteristic curve tracers. 0.3 This standard COVCI'S methods cf measurements on the characteristics of cathode-ray oscilloscope under t!ie ib!lowing headings: a) Vertical deflection performance, and of the following characteristics b) Horizontal dellection performance, c) R/lisccllane.xs characteristics. 0.3.1 Procedures for the measurement are untier considcraticu: a) Delay in vertical dcdrction system, b) Intensity (Z) modulation, and c) .\mplitudc calibration. 0.3.2 Proccdurzs for the measurement of the characteristics cathode-ray cxil!oscnpes are under consideration. 3 OL triggered

1:4334-1967 0.4 This standard lays down a single method of measurement for each characteristic so as to achieve the required degree of precision. It is not, however, intended to exclude other alternative methods of measurement for which necessary measuring equipment may be available and which are of equal or greater precision than the method prescribed in this standard. 0.5 The requirements of the different classes of oscilloscope are proposed to be covered in a series of standards, the first among them covering requirements for general purpose cathode-ray oscilloscope is under consideration. 0.6 In view of the fact that the markings on the oscilloscope indicating the model, designation, component location, current consumption, rated voltage and other significant particulars are helpful in conducting measurements, it was felt desirable to include a clause on information required by the testing authorities in Appendix A. 0.7 In reporting the result of a test made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard lays down the conditions and procedures for the tests to be conducted on cathode-ray oscilloscopes covering ranges between dc and 10 MC/S to determine their performance characteristics. 1.1.1 These tests apply to complete oscilloscopes only and not to component parts thereof. 1.1.2 This standard does not apply to special construction or special purpose oscilloscopes, such as sampling oscilloscopes, vectorscopes and characteristic curve tracers. 2. 2.4.1 Sweep - The horizontal trace of the spgt, produced by the deflection of the electron beam, on the screen. Thu is generally achieved by feeding a saw-tooth wave to the horizontal plates of the cathode-ray tube from the time base. 2.4.2 Nonlinearity of Sweep - Maximum departure from the average rate of rise (slope ) of the saw-tooth wave, applied to the horizontal plates. This factor is expressed in percentage:' Nonlinearity of sweep = Maximum departure Average uniform of slope rate x loo slope rate of the display or

2.4.4 Expansion ( or Magnification ) - The process of increasing sweep speed, for example, by increasing the gain of the horizontal amplifier resulting in an expansion of a part of the unexpanded display. 2.4.5 Synchronked Sweep or Locked Sweep - A recurrent sweep synchronized so as to maintain the sweep period equal to, or to a multiple of. the period of the observed `quantity. 2 .I .6 Trigpcred Sweep -A ( positive or negative ) and need not be regular. sweep having which is initiated a rest position. by a trigger The repetition pulse rate

2.4.7 Internal Synchronkation ( or `Triggering ) - The synchronization ( or triggering) obtained when the signal which controls the time base is supplied by an internal circuit influenced by the observed quantity. 2.4.8 External S,vchronization ( or Triggering ) - The synchronization ( or triggerirrg ) obtamed when the signal which controls the time base is applied externally and independently of internal circuits influenced by the observed quantity. 2.4.9 Synchronkation ( or Triggering ) Frequency Range - The frequency range fcr which the internal or external synchronizatron ( or triggering ) circuits permit a stable display. 7

IS:433091967 2.4.10 Synchronization ( or Triggering ) Thrsshoid - The minimum value of the synchronizing ( or triggering ) signal ( external ) or the minimum value of the vertical deflection ( internal ) which is necessarv to obtain a stable display. 3. GENERAL CONDlTIONS FOR MEASUREMENTS

3.0 Unless otherwise specified, measurements shall be made under normal measuring conditions as specified in 3.1 to 3.5. 3.1 Normal Supply Voltpae cathode-ray oscilloscopt Rated voltage shall be applied to the

3.1.1 The voltage applied to the cathode-ray oscilloscope shall be held constant within 2-O percent of the rated value during the measurement of the characteristics. 3.4.2 In case of ac lnams operation, the voltage shall be applied at the rated frequency. The harmonic content of ac mains supply voltage shall not exceed 5-O percent. 3.1.3 In case of battery operation, primary or secondary batteries of the type and rated voltage as specified by the manufacturer, shall be used. 3.2 Standard Atmospheric Conditions for Tests

3.2.1 Unless otherwise specined, all tests shall be carried out under the following atmospheric conditions: Between 15'C and 35�C Temperature Relative humidity Atmosphlric pressure Between 45 percent and 75 percent Between 860 mbar and 1 060 mbar

3.2.1.1 Where the conditions mentioned above have a significant influence, these shall be kept substantially constant during the test. 3.2.2 If the temperature limits as given in 3.2.1 are too wide for certain tests, these shall be conducted, or repeated in case of doubt, at a temoerature of 27 f 1�C and relative humidity of 65 f 2 percent. 3.2.3 The radiations. instrument shall be protected from draughts and direct

4. PERFORMANCE
4.1 Sensitivity

OF

VERTICAL

SYSTEM

- The sensitivity of the vertical deflection system shall be measured at a specified frequency at various calibrated values of sensitivity. A known magnitude ( peak-to-peak value ) of signal shall be fed to the vertical deflection input terminals of the cathode-ray oscilloscope so that the deflection of the waveform on the screen is about 80 percent of the The magnitude of the signal deflection appearing on the measuring area. screen shall be measured accurately. The sensitivity shall be computed from these measurements.

4.2 Linearity - The sensitivity of the vertical deflection system shall be measured as specified in 4.1 for various levels of input to the vertical deflection system starting from a signal input required for full deflection over the measuring area and reducing in suitable steps, At least five shall be made. measurements In case of dc operated cathode-ray oscilloscopes, the measurements shall be done both for positive and negative deflections. The linearity error shall be computed as the maximum percentage deviation of the sensitivities at different levels from the sensitivity measured in 4.1 (that is, sensitivity at about 80 percent deflection ) . deflection system of the 4.3 Frequency Response - With the vertical cathode-ray oscilloscope set at one of the calibrated sensitivity points, the sensitivity shall be measured at suitable iqtervals over the entire specified frequency range at a constant signal input level which does not overload the vertical deflection system of the cathode-ray oscilloscope. The sensitivity The measurethus measured shall be plotted as a function of frequency. ments shall be repeated for different calibrated sensitivities. 4.4 Square Wave Response-Square wave response shall be checked for all the values of calibrated sensitivities. A pulse ( having a rise time of about 0*3t and of duration not less than lot, where t is the rise time of vertical deflection system of cathode-ray oscilloscope ) of suitable magnitude 9

IS : 4330 - 1967 to produce a deflection of at least 80 percent o: tne measuring area shall be applied to the input terminals of the vertical deflection system. For this test the impedance of the pulse generator and the input circuit cathode-ray oscilloscope of the including the connecting cables shall be matched properly. The values of rise or fall time, overshoot ahd sag shall be measured ( see 2.3.6 ). The squarewave response measurements shall be carridd out at pulse repetition frequencies corresponding to the lower and upper limit of the sweep frequency, the upper limit being limited to such a frequency that its third harmonic does not exceed the vertical amplifier bandwidth.
NOTE - This mcsurement incorporating a delay line. is ::pplicable only to the cathode-ray oscillmcopes

4.5 Input Impedance 4.5.1 nc Input Impedance -The input impedance shall be measured over the specified frequency range and expressed in term of its equivalent parallel resistive and reactive components as a function of frequency, The measurements may be made with a Q-meter. The input terminals of the vertical deflection system shall be connected to the capacitance terminals of a *meter which is tuned for resonance at a frequency of, say, 100 kc/s, with a suitable inductor. The magnification factor Q, and the capacitance C, shall be noted. The Q-meter shall be retuned for resonance after disconnecting the oscilloscope terminals and the magnification factor ( Qz) and capacitance (C.J are again noted. The input capacitance and resistance of the vertical deflecTion system of the cathode-ray oscilloscope is given by a) Input capacitance = C, - C, b) Input resistance = 2J Ci-( Q2 .-

The input terminals of the vertical and horizontal deflection systems shall be short-circuited and the sweep circuit switched off. The spot is then acccrately focussed and the oscilloscope operated for a period corresponding to that specified for long term drift. During this period, the position of the spot is recorded either by direct measurenient or by a photographic recording device, at intervals of time corresponding to that specified for short term drift. From the record obtained, the long term drift and short term drift are computed. NOTE- This mu:asuremcnt covcr.~ both the Oertical and horizontal deflection

The linearity `error shall be computed from these measurements. 5.1.3 Internal Synchronizing Threshold - With the set-up for sweep-rate measurement ( Jee 5.1.1), the synchronizing control, the input signal and the frequency of the signal generator shall be adjusted to determine the minimum input signal which when increased from zero level produces a stationary pattern. The input level thus obtained corresponds to the internal synchronizing threshold level. 5.1.4 External Synchronizing Threshold L.evel -The measurement shall be made as specified in 5.1.3 except that the cathode-ray oscilloscope shall be set at its external synchronizing position and `the output of the signal generator shall be fed also to the external synchronizing terminals. 5.1.5 Sweep Znstubifity - The sweep instability sha!l be checked at all settings of the sweep rate control. During these measurements, the supply voltage shall be kept constant within 1.0 percent, the supply frequency within 1-O percent, the ambient temperatures at 27 f 1�C and relative This measurement shall be done with the humidity at 65 f 2 percent. synchronizing system put out of action. A sinusoidal signal of the known frequency shall be fed into the input terminals of the vertical amplifier deflection system. The sweep rate control shall be adjusted to obtain a practically steady pattern and the cathode-ray oscilloscope is operated for a period corresponding to that specified for long term drift. Any drift in the pattern shall be stabilized by adjusting the input frequency, The difference between the initiai and final frequency will be a measure of the sweep drift. The drift shall be measured at intervals of time corresponding to that specified for short term drift over the specified period for long term drift. 5.1.6 Jitter - The jitter shall be measured at the synchronizing threshold level ( both internal and external ), at the highest sweep rate and highest sensitivity of the vertial deflection system. A sinusoidal wave, the amplitude of which is equal to 25 percent of the measuring area, shall be fed into the input terminals of the vertical deflection system. The frequency of the input signal shall be adjusted so as to obtain one complete sinusoidal trace on the screen and the horizontal movement of the trace on the horizontal axis shall be measured. Jitter shall be measured as a percentage of full sweep length. 12

6.1 Phase DiEerence Between Vertical and Horizontal Deflection
between the vertical and horizontal systems - The phase difference deflection systems shall be determined by applying the same signal to the input terminals of the vertical and horizontal deflection systems. This test shall be made in a frequency range indicated by the manufacturer. 6.1.1 A sine wave signal of a frequency, say 1 kc/s and amplitude 1 volt shali be applied to the input terminals of the vertical and horizontal deflection systems with the controls adjusted to get a deflection of 4 cm in each axis on the screen. Without phase difference a straight line is observed on the screen. With mutual phase shift this straight !ine becomes an ellipse (see Fig. 2 ). 6.4 Expansion Factor -The expansion factor shall be measured at various calibrated values of the expansion control. The sweep control shall first be set at an appropriate calibrated position and from a pulse generator, pulses CJfknown duration shall be fed to the input terminals of the vertical deflection system so that sufficient number of pulses appear on the screen over the specified measuring area. The pulse duration should be of such a magnitude as to produce trace width ( of each pulse ) of at least 5 mm 15

`F : 4330 - 1967 The sweep control shall then be adjusted to obtain on the screen. The width of the pulses shall be measured initially and stationary pattern. From these measurements, at various positions of the expansion control. the expansion factor shall bc computed.
